summary: New 802.1X CA rotation prevented recent endpoints from establishing corporate VPN over office Wi-Fi
description:
Issue summary:
After a scheduled CA/intermediate certificate rotation on our RADIUS/802.1X stack, a number of recently provisioned laptops failed to establish the corporate VPN when connected to office Wi-Fi. 802.1X association completed and DHCP was assigned; however VPN negotiation (IKEv2) repeatedly failed with certificate validation errors.

Impact:
~22 employees in SF office unable to initiate VPN over Wi‑Fi between 2026-03-10 08:15 and 2026-03-10 11:30 local time. Devices on wired network or cellular could connect successfully. Affected users were mostly new joiners provisioned in the last 4 weeks. No production services were impacted.

Environment:
- RADIUS: FreeRADIUS cluster behind F5, certificates rotated via automation runbook (rotate-ca.sh) at 2026-03-10 07:50 PST.
- VPN gateway: strongSwan-based IKEv2 endpoints (redwood-vpn-1/2) in us-west.
- Endpoints: mix of macOS 13/14 and Windows 11 corporate images provisioned via MDM.
- Wi-Fi controllers: Aruba controllers with 802.1X profile pointing to RADIUS pool.

Expected behavior:
New cert rotation should be transparent to already-provisioned endpoints and new endpoints that have the updated CA trust via MDM.

Actual behavior:
Endpoints that were provisioned in the last 30 days fail IKE auth with messages indicating untrusted client certificate or chain mismatch. Older endpoints and wired-connected devices succeed.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Provision a new corporate laptop with MDM profile pushed but before scheduled CA trust update applied.
2) Connect to office Wi‑Fi and complete 802.1X authentication (observed to succeed).
3) Attempt to start VPN via built-in IKEv2 profile.
4) Observe VPN negotiation failure repeating immediately after IKE_SA_INIT / IKE_AUTH.

Logs / evidence:
- strongSwan log excerpt (vpn gateway): "charon: 12[CFG] certificate verification failed for 'CN=device-123,OU=endpoints' - reason: unknown_ca"
- FreeRADIUS auth log: user EAP TLS OK (802.1X stage), shows server cert chain served from rotated CA chain.
- Windows Event Viewer (NetworkProfile): "IKE_AUTH failed with error 0x80090325 (SEC_E_CERT_EXPIRED)" for a new joiner device.
- macOS Console (racoon/charon): "peer certificate chain does not chain to trusted root"
- Automation job rotate-ca.sh ran at 07:50 and updated RADIUS server certs, but MDM CA push job (mdm/push-ca) scheduled for 09:00 failed for some devices (see mdm job failure ids).

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: rotation introduced a new intermediate CA not present in endpoint trust stores. Confirmed by inspecting cert chain from RADIUS and comparing to MDM CA bundle.
- Verified that RADIUS and VPN certs were using the new chain; freeRADIUS sends full chain but endpoints validate against their local trust store which lacked the new intermediate.
- Why only recent devices? New images are built to only trust the narrow CA bundle provided at provisioning; older devices had the broader historical CA store. MDM push job showed ~30% failure rate during the scheduled rollout due to an intermittent device-side MDM agent issue.
- Workaround discovered: connecting via wired Ethernet allowed SCEP client renewal to fetch and install the intermediate during provisioning flow. Cellular tethering also worked.
- Peer test: created a temporary VPN endpoint that accepted certificate chain anchored to the old CA and verified those affected devices could connect. Rolling back RADIUS to old chain restored connectivity for everyone immediately.
- Root cause: automated CA rotation executed before confirming MDM rollout completion; lack of staged canary and device-level validation in the runbook.

Actions taken during incident:
- 08:25 - Triage call in #internal-network, incident owner assigned to Diego Ramos.
- 08:40 - Identified correlation between rotate-ca job and first VPN failures.
- 08:55 - Rolled back RADIUS/VPN TLS chain to previous CA on all RADIUS nodes to restore connectivity (temporary roll-back).
- 09:10 - Created targeted MDM retry job for failed devices (mdm/push-ca retry) and manual intervention queue for machines that did not auto-apply the CA.
- 10:20 - Confirmed affected users could connect via Wi‑Fi after rollback.
- 11:00 - Re-executed rotation with staggered rollout and verification hooks; verified MDM push succeeded for sample cohort via device logs.
- 11:30 - Rotation completed with updated runbook controls and monitoring; incident declared resolved.

Comments:
- "Aisha Patel (reporter): Noticed multiple new joiners hitting this at 08:10; they were blocked on internal tools and support queue filled quickly. Pushed for rollback asap." (Slack #it-support)
- "Diego Ramos (assignee): Rolled back RADIUS cert chain at 08:55; will coordinate root cause and follow-up. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/981" (Slack #internal-network)
- "Jules Kim (Endpoint Eng): MDM agent had a known regression in 2.18.3 that caused CA pushes to hang on devices with fresh images. Filed INT-14801 to patch agent across fleet." (internal-support)
- "SRE note: Added an alert to detect simultaneous failures of VPN auth + 802.1X OK within 5m window to catch this faster." (Diego)

Related links and artifacts:
- Slack: #internal-network thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123456789/p1678579200000000
- Infra PR for rollback & staged rotation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/981
- Confluence runbook (updated): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/IT/pages/8021X+CA+Rotation+Runbook
- Linked issue: INT-14801 (MDM agent patch)

Resolution summary:
- Immediate: Rolled back RADIUS/VPN certificate chain to previous trusted CA at 08:55, restoring VPN for affected devices.
- Short-term: Re-ran CA rotation with staged rollout, targeted MDM retries, and manual remediation for devices that failed to apply the CA.
- Long-term: Runbook updated to include pre-rotation MDM verification step, canary subset, automated rollback on >5% auth failures, and a post-rotation health check that validates VPN establishment for recent-provisioned endpoints.

Follow-up / action items:
- INT-14801: rollout MDM agent 2.18.4 and re-run CA push for remaining devices. (Jules Kim)
- INT-14802: add automated canary validation to rotate-ca.sh to verify MDM trust distribution before switching RADIUS (Diego Ramos)
- Update internal runbook and postmortem doc in Confluence. (Aisha Patel)

Resolution:
- Status: Resolved on 2026-03-12 after completing staggered rotation and MDM fixes. Root cause: premature CA rotation without validating MDM propagation; contributing factor: MDM agent regression on new images.
